maria_chen: Heads-up — Acme Health asked what exact outbound firewall rules they must open for Redwood Private (on-prem) so our control plane + model fetches work. They are VERY locked down and prefer IP allowlists only (no proxy).

oliver_k: Short answer: recommend a customer-managed HTTP(S) CONNECT proxy if possible. If they can only do IPs, we can offer a static egress IP add-on, otherwise IPs may be large/ephemeral.

oliver_k: Key pieces to explain to security:
- Our control plane and S3/model downloads use TLS on 443 (SNI to hostnames).
- We push telemetry/metrics to ingestion endpoints over 443.
- Model artifacts may be hosted on cloud object storage (S3/GCS) — those endpoints can resolve to many IPs.

suman: Full list of pragmatic options for them: 
1) Proxy (recommended): configure HTTPS proxy with CONNECT and allowlist that appliance to talk to 443 outbound. Our agent supports standard env vars: 
```
HTTPS_PROXY=http://proxy.corp.local:3128
NO_PROXY=localhost,127.0.0.1,169.254.169.254
```
Works for downloads, control plane, image pulls.

2) FQDN-based allowlist: allow outbound TCP:443 to these FQDNs (if their firewall supports FQDN):
- control.redwood.ai
- models.redwood.ai
- artifacts.redwood-inference.com
- ingest.telemetry.redwood.ai
- packaging.s3.amazonaws.com (or equivalent cloud storage host)
This keeps their IP surface small conceptually but relies on DNS/SNI rules on the firewall.

3) IP allowlist (least preferred unless they buy static egress):
- If they accept dynamic cloud egress, we must warn that cloud provider IPs change and CDNs fronting models can expand ranges.
- If they require strict IPs, opt into our "static egress pool" add-on (contact sales). That gives you 2-4 /24s per region with guaranteed stable NAT IPs we announce.

jessica_ops: For teams who still want an example minimal set to start testing (non-production, temporary):
- Allow outbound TCP 443 to these example addresses (note: these are sample endpoints and may change):
```
34.82.120.55/32  # control.redwood.ai (example)
34.82.121.0/24   # models edge (example)
52.216.45.8/32   # artifacts mirror (example)
```
Do NOT treat these as a produced allowlist — thats why we push FQDN/proxy option.

maria_chen: Also call out other ports/services they often forget:
- Port 123 (NTP) if nodes need time sync to external NTP (or use internal NTP).
- DNS (UDP 53) to their resolver — if they block DNS, agent fails to resolve FQDN.
- Optional outbound 443 to telemetry endpoint; if blocked we fall back to buffered telemetry (but support/alerts will be degraded).

oliver_k: Helpful tests they can run to validate connectivity: 
1) TLS handshake + SNI check:
```
openssl s_client -connect control.redwood.ai:443 -servername control.redwood.ai
```
2) Fetch a small model manifest:
```
curl -v https://models.redwood.ai/v1/manifest --resolve models.redwood.ai:443:34.82.121.12
```
3) Proxy test: set HTTPS_PROXY and run `curl https://control.redwood.ai/health`

suman: Internal note for us — if customer chooses IP-only and refuses add-on, we should:
- Put them on a 30-day review ticket to monitor broken downloads as cloud IPs change.
- Provide automation to push updated IP lists to their firewall via API (if they have SD-WAN).

jessica_ops: FYI — in cases where customers run air-gapped/on-prem with no egress, we support a pull-mirror option: they can ship a tarball of model artifacts to a private registry we provide instructions for. Thats a separate onboarding path.

sre-bot: ACTION CREATED: KB-1482 "Customer egress guidance — on-prem" assigned to oliver_k. Due 2026-04-02 :spiral_calendar:

maria_chen: I'll paste this guidance to the customer. If they push back on proxy, we should escalate with sales for static egress quote. :thumbsup:

oliver_k: Thanks — add a short one-pager with the recommended firewall rules and the proxy snippet. I'll update KB-1482 with the add-on pricing link and exact static IP ranges once legal signs the allocation.

jessica_ops: Also add a little troubleshooting checklist (DNS, proxy auth, TLS interception) — we've seen TLS MITM by corporate appliances break SNI validation and cause agent errors.

maria_chen: Perfect. Closing the loop here.
